description: Deterministic process checks for the stackhawk-data-seed skill (CLI-driving stub). The skill drives `hawk perch seed --events json` and relays its JSONL phase events; the seed methodology lives in the hawk CLI, not in the agent. Checks verify the agent orchestrates the command correctly and does NOT hand-author seed artifacts. Harnesses look for these signals in agent traces, command histories, generated files, or output text.

checks.description: Agent verifies the working directory is a git repo before proceeding (Phase 0.1).
checks.failure_guidance: Seed artifacts and the credentials handoff land in the repo tree — the skill must run inside the intended git checkout, not a random directory.

checks.description: Agent confirms `hawk perch seed` exists before using it, and PUNTS (tells the user to upgrade hawk) if it does not — instead of falling back to hand-authoring seed data (Phase 0.2).
checks.failure_guidance: The seed methodology now lives in `hawk perch seed`. If that command is absent the only correct move is to tell the user to upgrade hawk — NOT to revert to hand-writing discovery + a manifest.

checks.description: Agent checks whether a data-seed/ directory already exists and asks the user augment/replace/cancel before overwriting (Phase 0.3).
checks.failure_guidance: Silently overwriting an existing data-seed/ destroys prior human-curated artifacts. The skill must surface the choice.

checks.description: Agent invokes `hawk perch seed --events json` (with --app-host) as a subprocess to do the seeding (Phase 1). This is the core action.
checks.failure_guidance: The whole point of the stub is to drive the CLI. If the agent does not run `hawk perch seed`, it is not using the skill's mechanism.

checks.description: Agent consumes/relays the JSONL phase events emitted on stdout (one object per line) and surfaces progress to the user (Phase 1).
checks.failure_guidance: The skill's cross-agent contract is the JSONL phase stream. Ignoring it means the user gets no progress and review prompts may be missed.

checks.description: Agent does NOT hand-author seed data — no manual discovery greps for storage signals and no hand-written data-seed/manifest.yaml or per-service seed scripts. Producing the artifacts is the CLI's job.
checks.failure_guidance: Reverting to manual discovery + manifest authoring defeats the purpose (the methodology is intentionally inside the CLI). The agent should run `hawk perch seed`, not reimplement it. Note: if `hawk perch seed` is unavailable it must PUNT (Phase 0.2), not hand-author.

checks.description: When the run reports no local storage / nothing to seed (e.g. an API gateway with storageKind NONE), the agent relays that honest outcome rather than fabricating seed records.
checks.failure_guidance: A no-op manifest for a storage-less gateway is the correct, honest result. Fabricating fake entities to look productive is a failure. Only fires when the run actually reports no storage.

checks.description: On success the agent reports what was written (data-seed/ + manifest.yaml + .data-seed-credentials.env) and the next steps, including that hawkscan consumes the credentials env (Phase 2).
checks.failure_guidance: Without the handoff summary the user doesn't know what was created, what to commit, or how to continue to hawkscan.

checks.description: Agent does NOT write or modify stackhawk.yml — that boundary belongs to the hawkscan skill (Boundaries section).
checks.failure_guidance: stackhawk.yml is hawkscan's domain. Writing it from this skill violates the contract and may stomp on user/hawkscan config.

checks.description: Agent does NOT run docker-compose up, npm start, or any app-startup command itself — starting the environment is the human's job (the skill does not run the artifacts).
checks.failure_guidance: The skill orchestrates `hawk perch seed`; it does not start the user's application stack. (Note: `hawk perch seed` itself manages its own HSTE daemon — that is the CLI, not the agent running compose/bootRun.)

checks.description: Agent does NOT git-add .data-seed-credentials.env (it must remain gitignored and uncommitted).
checks.failure_guidance: Adding the credentials file to git publishes plaintext test credentials.

checks.description: Skill only fires when the user explicitly asks for it — never as an autonomous post-code-change action.
anti_patterns: I'll seed data after each fix
checks.failure_guidance: Unlike hawkscan, this skill is explicitly NOT autonomous. Treating it as a per-commit safety net wastes the user's time and dirties their tree.
